findings.evidence: The active workflow explains that "a double-quoted expansion is never re-parsed" after giving the exact loader and argument forms. That general Bash explanation adds little beyond the adapter-specific rule.
findings.fix: Keep the exact loader and the rule to pass stored JSON as a quoted argument, never pasted into a command. Move the general shell explanation to references/design-notes.md.

findings.evidence: "a live-quota-checked (runtime, model) pair for each task's implementer dispatch (native or external CLI)" overstates coverage: native choices can skip quota probes, and session-model mode uses no named pair. "execute or run a superpowers plan that way" also leaves resuming or finishing an existing adapter run implicit.
findings.fix: Use when asked to run or resume an existing Superpowers implementation plan task by task with subagents, even if the user does not name subagent-driven-development, or when ai-kit-spec-execute routes a plan here. Resolve each task's native or external CLI implementer, check quota where applicable, and handle waits and fix-round escalation. Start the plan's unit branch and finish the same run after final review by folding and, with consent, publishing it through ai-kit-commit-fold. Applies to docs/superpowers/plans/*.md; not for GSD, inline superpowers:executing-plans, or standalone branch folding.

findings.evidence: The native path links to "host-config audit" inside references/dispatch-external-cli.md, but line 262 says "Do NOT load it for mode == \"native\"." The shared audit has no unambiguous load rule for native dispatch.
findings.fix: Put the shared audit contract in references/host-config-audit.md. Link it from both branches when interpreting audit output, and keep the external dispatch recipe gated to external_cli.

findings.evidence: "Do NOT load it at any other point" conflicts with Step 2's use of config-check.md block 3 and Step 5's instruction to recover the exact notice from that file. The same blanket restriction appears inside the reference.
findings.fix: Give the file three explicit triggers: read the check and record blocks before start, read block 3 only when CONFIG_CHECK is once or notice, and read just the corresponding notice when closing such a run. Keep the existing recipes in that reference.

findings.evidence: "Every other exec target has full permissions, and its stay-in-the-target-dir guidance is not a boundary." The skill explains the risk but gives no pre-dispatch rule for a workspace whose required write boundary the chosen lane cannot enforce.
findings.fix: Before spawning, compare the lane's effective write scope with the workspace's required boundary. If the boundary cannot be met, don't launch or silently change lanes; ask the owner for an isolated environment or an approved compatible pair.

findings.evidence: The flagged-quota eval mocks executor-fallback as {"switched": true, "key": "execute-backup"}, but the documented shell block reads the required "exclude" field. The eval then supplies a successful restricted re-resolution without supplying the data needed for that restriction.
findings.fix: Make the fake return "exclude": ["execute-primary"], and assert that resolve-injection receives that list with --no-fallback before execute-backup is dispatched.

findings.evidence: The positive "run my superpowers plan under subagent-driven-development" is representative: all ten positives name Superpowers or its workflow explicitly. The strong near-miss negatives are not matched by positives that rely on user intent or plan context alone.
findings.fix: Replace two explicit positives with realistic requests that rely on an already identified implementation plan, such as asking to hand each task to a fresh worker or to resume a paused implementer with its saved model. Keep the inline and standalone-fold negatives.

findings.evidence: The pinned write runs "write-resumable-state" and then unconditionally prints "RESUME_STATE_PATH=". If the write fails, the final printf masks the failure. Schedule-or-stop can announce a wake whose Restore step finds a missing or stale pin. The unpinned write at lines 181–182 has the same failure.
findings.fix: Check the write's exit status and verify that the saved state matches the current plan, task and expected pin before printing the path or arming a wake. If persistence fails, stop with the actual error and schedule nothing.

findings.evidence: "the runner reuses its session only when the task digest matches" is presented as the reason this wake can resume the prior session. But this adapter always uses sandboxed Codex exec, for which ai-kit-cross-ai/SKILL.md:278 and the runner's sameSessionArgv explicitly say there is no resume form. An unchanged digest preserves task identity, not the Codex session.
findings.fix: Keep the objective byte-identical and the runtime/model pinned, but distinguish a re-dispatch from a confirmed session resume. For sandboxed Codex, tell the owner it starts a fresh CLI session and use the runner's session and tree evidence before claiming continuity.

findings.evidence: "A refusal changes nothing, so the branch stays where it was" is not true for all checkpoint or ready failures. ai-kit-commit-fold's adapter guide says a catch-up push can already have happened; its checkpoint also folds before publishing, so a later publication failure need not undo the local fold.
findings.fix: Keep the stop and no-manual-move rules, but do not promise rollback. On refusal, report the failed stage and verify the current local tip, recorded unit state, and remote or PR state as applicable before telling the owner what completed and what to retry.

findings.evidence: "fold.py boundary --next ... has no --repo" is contradicted by the shipped `fold.py boundary --help`, which lists both `--next` and `[--repo REPO]`. Step 1 repeats the incorrect explanation.
findings.fix: Keep the prohibition on --next during an active unit: it writes a next-unit brief in place of the current one. Correct both mentions to say that omitting --repo defaults to the current directory, and keep the unit-scoped wave command with --repo "$CWD".

findings.evidence: "subprocess dispatch needs Node 24 (GSD's declared floor; older versions untested)" turns a dependency's declared floor into an adapter-wide requirement. The Evidence section names a package and version but gives no URL or check date. The published GSD manifest does declare >=24.0.0; that does not establish the standalone runner's minimum.
findings.fix: Separate GSD's declared requirement from the adapter's tested runtime range. Cite https://registry.npmjs.org/@opengsd%2fgsd-core/1.17.0 with the check date in Evidence, and state an adapter-wide minimum only if the adapter declares or enforces it.

findings.evidence: ".git writes unverified" leaves the user without a reliable rule for a lane expected to commit. OpenAI's current sandbox documentation explicitly lists .git and the Git directory behind a worktree pointer as protected in the default workspace-write policy. The skill provides no dated source or live check for the effective policy.
findings.fix: Link the official https://developers.openai.com/codex/agent-approvals-security#protected-paths-in-writable-roots in Evidence with the check date. Before dispatching a task that must commit, verify the installed lane's effective policy; if Git metadata is read-only, stop for an owner-approved commit path. The documentation was checked; no live provider dispatch or end-to-end eval was run in this read-only review.
